checks.description: State the business question or decision that the report is intended to support.

questions.ask: Does the report explicitly state a business question or a decision it supports?

checks.reason_template: An explicit business question or decision is stated: {question_stated}.

examples.text: Revenue was 1.2M. Costs were 0.8M.
examples.why: The report gives figures without a question or decision.

examples.text: We assess whether to expand the pilot to all stores.
examples.why: The intended decision is explicit.

checks.description: A material metric needs a formula or definition, a measurement window, and the population measured.

questions.ask: Does the claim use a metric as support for a conclusion?
Does the report define the metric, its time window, and the population it covers?

checks.reason_template: Metric "{metric_used.quote}" has a complete definition, time window, and population: {definition_complete}.

examples.text: Engagement increased by 15%.
examples.why: Engagement has no definition, window, or population in the report.

examples.text: Weekly engagement, the share of active app users opening the app at least twice, rose to 45% in Q3.
examples.why: Definition, window, and population are supplied.

checks.description: Check the metric against the official EJ definition once that definition is supplied.
checks.pending_question: What is EJ's official definition of this metric?

checks.description: Disclose the data source, sample size, and time range needed to interpret the results.

questions.ask: Does the report disclose the data source, sample size, and covered dates?

checks.reason_template: Data source, sample size, and time range are all disclosed: {disclosure_complete}.

examples.text: Our survey shows higher satisfaction.
examples.why: The source details, sample size, and dates are absent.

examples.text: We analyzed 320 responses from the July 2025 customer survey.
examples.why: Source, sample size, and time range are given.

checks.description: Comparisons must use comparable populations and periods or explain adjustments for seasonal effects and period length.

questions.ask: Does this claim compare outcomes between periods or populations?
Are the populations and periods comparable, or are material differences adjusted or explicitly accounted for?

checks.reason_template: Comparison "{comparison_made.quote}" accounts for material population or period differences: {comparable}.

examples.text: December revenue exceeded a one-week January sample, so performance improved.
examples.why: Period lengths and seasonal effects are not accounted for.

examples.text: Revenue per trading day rose versus the same month last year across the same stores.
examples.why: Comparable windows and stores are specified.

checks.description: Causal wording must be backed by a control group or identification strategy.

questions.ask: Does the claim state that X caused, drove, or led to Y?
What comparison or identification strategy does the report use to support this claim?

checks.reason_template: Causal wording "{causal_wording.quote}" is supported only by: {comparison}.

examples.text: The new training raised output by 12%.
examples.why: Before/after only, no control group.

examples.text: Output rose 12% versus a matched control site.
examples.why: A control group is present.

checks.description: A small difference described as significant needs a variability or significance explanation.

questions.ask: Does the claim describe a small observed difference as significant or decisive?
Does the report provide variability, uncertainty, or significance evidence supporting that wording?

checks.reason_template: Significance wording "{significance_claimed.quote}" includes supporting uncertainty or significance evidence: {uncertainty_explained}.

examples.text: A 0.1-point increase is a decisive improvement.
examples.why: No variability or significance evidence is supplied.

examples.text: The difference was 0.1 points, with a 95% confidence interval from -0.2 to 0.4, so improvement is uncertain.
examples.why: The uncertainty limits the interpretation.

checks.description: Recompute an explicit addition equation and flag a result outside the defined rounding tolerance.
Check an unambiguous stated percentage change against the start and end values and its direction.
A referenced table, figure, exhibit, or appendix must have a corresponding heading or caption in the report.
Numbers need units, a time range, and an applicable denominator or base.

questions.ask: Does the claim use a numerical measure?
Are its units, time range, and any necessary denominator or base clear from the report?

checks.reason_template: Number "{number_used.quote}" has sufficient units, period, and base: {context_complete}.

examples.text: The rate reached 20.
examples.why: The unit, period, and base are unclear.

examples.text: In Q3, 20% of the 500 active accounts renewed.
examples.why: The unit, period, and denominator are supplied.

checks.description: A recommendation should cite or clearly follow from a finding in this report.

questions.ask: Does the claim recommend a business action?
Can the proposed action be traced to a relevant finding in this report?

checks.reason_template: Recommendation "{recommendation_made.quote}" is traceable to a reported finding: {finding_supports}.

examples.text: We should double the advertising budget.
examples.why: The report contains no finding about advertising.

examples.text: Because the pilot reduced processing delays, extend it to the other two sites.
examples.why: The action is tied to the reported pilot finding.

checks.description: A certain promise about future outcomes needs supporting grounds; an expectation alone is not a guarantee.

questions.ask: Does the claim promise a future outcome with certainty?
Does the report provide grounds sufficient for the stated certainty?

checks.reason_template: Future certainty "{guarantee_wording.quote}" has supporting grounds in the report: {grounds_present}.

examples.text: This initiative guarantees that revenue will double next year.
examples.why: No grounds support the certainty.

examples.text: We expect higher revenue if adoption reaches 60%, but the outcome remains uncertain.
examples.why: This is a conditional expectation rather than a guarantee.

checks.description: Disclose material assumptions behind forecasts and plans.

questions.ask: Does the report present a forecast or a future business plan?
Does the report state the material assumptions that the forecast or plan depends on?

checks.reason_template: Forecast or plan "{forecast_or_plan.quote}" discloses its material assumptions: {assumptions_disclosed}.

examples.text: The plan projects 25% growth next year.
examples.why: No demand, capacity, or adoption assumptions are stated.

examples.text: The plan projects 25% growth if demand rises 10% and the second site opens in June.
examples.why: The projection states its dependencies.

checks.description: Determine whether escalation is required once the official EJ process is supplied.
checks.pending_question: What is the EJ escalation process and which thresholds apply to this review?
